summary: engine-audio phase A is closed. The transcription is calibrated, the decoder has been improved, bundle hygiene is proven and the audio paths are verified. (1) I added 5 REAL-piano fixtures, rendered with Node and ffmpeg from the offline FluidR3_GM samples (scripts/fixtures/make-piano-fixtures.mjs, deterministic, no sox needed): piano-melody, piano-chords, piano-arpeggio, piano-chords-room and piano-arpeggio-room. The old sox fixtures (pluck synth) scored 0.98 mean F1, but these exposed real-piano accuracy of only 0.78. (2) Two decoder bugs were found from dumped activations and fixed in src/engine/transcribe/onsets.ts. (a) evaluateModel stitches ~2 s windows every 142 frames (1.65 s), and frame activations jump at each seam. Basic Pitch's frame-difference onset inference turned every held note crossing a seam into a duplicated note. Frame differences now never straddle a seam; real attacks on a seam still come through the onset head. (b) Low notes have double-peaked onsets ~50 ms apart, and the decoder walks backwards, so the late peak won and the true onset was dropped. Same-pitch onsets within +/-5 frames (58 ms) now collapse into the strongest. There is also a measured bass bonus: onset thresholds are 15 % lower up to E2, easing to none at E3. (3) I recalibrated the sensitivity anchors. Onset is [0.85, 0.70, 0.45] and frame is [0.40, 0.30, 0.20] at sensitivity 0 / 0.5 / 1. Sensitivity 0.5 is the best mean F1, and the plateau is flat around it (0.65-0.725 / 0.25-0.325). The melodia pass is now always off, because on piano it adds overtones (F1 0.83 -> 0.72). FINAL TABLE at sensitivity 0.5, minNoteMs 90 (P / R / F1): scale 1.00/1.00/1.00, chords 1.00/0.88/0.93, melody-bass 0.92/1.00/0.96, scale.mp4 1.00/1.00/1.00, chords-room 1.00/1.00/1.00, melody-bass-room 0.92/1.00/0.96, piano-melody 1.00/0.97/0.99, piano-chords 0.86/0.75/0.80, piano-arpeggio 0.82/0.98/0.89, piano-chords-room 0.92/0.65/0.76, piano-arpeggio-room 0.85/0.97/0.90, silence.wav 0 notes. Mean F1: synthetic 0.971 (before 0.983), real piano 0.869 (before 0.784), all 0.920 (before 0.883). Onset bias is -4..+8 ms. Sensitivity sweep, mean F1 over all 10 calibration fixtures: s0 0.800, s0.2 0.879, s0.4 0.913, s0.5 0.920, s0.6 0.909, s0.8 0.883, s1 0.803. Note counts grow monotonically, about 2.3x from s0 to s1, and scale.wav F1 is 1.00 from s0 to s0.8. (4) Build proof: a throwaway build with the project's vite.config.ts takes two inputs, the app and a probe that imports the engines like the capture pipeline. Output is in my temp folder. The worker is its own chunk (worker-*.js, 1775 KiB, holding all tfjs and basic-pitch code). The engine client is 11 KiB, the app chunk is 566 KiB, and neither contains any tfjs or basic-pitch code. Re-runnable with node scripts/fixtures/check-bundle.mjs. (5) scale.mp4 decodes (kind video, 6.10 s), and silence.wav gives 0 notes. A fake-mic recording gives 8/8 scale notes, cancel() gives AbortError, and tab capture records. (6) Backends on this PC: headless Chrome does NOT use SwiftShader by default here. It gets the real GPU through ANGLE D3D11 (NVIDIA RTX 2060): model load + warm-up 7-10 s, then ~28x real time (30 s of audio in 1.06 s, 5 min in 7.7 s). With --gpu (ANGLE Vulkan): load 4.8 s, 35x real time. With --swiftshader (software WebGL): load 4.2 s, 1.4x real time (30 s in 22.2 s). The tfjs CPU backend runs at 0.7x real time. F1 is identical on every backend. Robustness: if WebGL warm-up fails, the worker now reloads the model on the CPU instead of failing.

public_api_notes:
AUDIO (import from src/engine/audio):
- decodeMediaFile(file: Blob, name?) -> Promise<DecodedMedia { buffer: AudioBuffer (device rate, e.g. 48000), duration (s), kind: 'audio'|'video' (from MIME, then extension), name (File.name or 'archivo'), mime }>. Decodes audio AND video containers (mp4 verified). On failure it throws an Error with name 'DecodeError' and message DECODE_ERROR_MESSAGE (exported) = 'No se pudo leer el audio de este archivo. Prueba con MP3, WAV, M4A o MP4.'. Show err.message in a toast.
- toModelInput(buffer, range?: { start, end } in seconds) -> Promise<Float32Array>: mono, MODEL_SAMPLE_RATE (22050), cropped, peak-normalized to 0.95. Pass it straight to transcribe().
- toMono(buffer, range?, sampleRate = buffer.sampleRate) -> Promise<Float32Array>, NOT normalized. encodeWav(samples, sampleRate) -> Blob 'audio/wav', 16-bit PCM mono. Trimmed file audio for keepOriginalAudio: encodeWav(await toMono(decoded.buffer, range, MODEL_SAMPLE_RATE), MODEL_SAMPLE_RATE) is ~43 KB per second.
- computePeaks(buffer, bins) -> Float32Array in 0..1, normalized to the loudest bin. Feed it to <Waveform peaks>.
- startRecording({ mode: 'mic'|'tab', onLevel?(level 0..1, ~30 Hz, fast attack / soft release), maxSeconds?, onAutoStop? }) -> Promise<RecorderHandle { stop(): Promise<Blob>, cancel(), startedAt }>. The blob is audio/webm;codecs=opus in Chrome and audio/mp4 in Safari. The mic opens with echoCancellation, noiseSuppression and autoGainControl off. At maxSeconds, onAutoStop fires and you still call stop() to get the blob. onAutoStop also fires when the user ends tab sharing from the browser UI. stop() and cancel() release every track and AudioContext. After cancel(), stop() rejects with AbortError ('Grabación cancelada.'). Errors by err.name, each with a Spanish err.message: NotAllowedError (mic 'Permite el acceso al micrófono para escuchar.' / tab 'No se compartió ninguna pestaña.'), NotFoundError ('No se encontró ningún micrófono.'), NotReadableError ('El micrófono está ocupado por otra aplicación.' / 'No se pudo capturar la pestaña.'), NotSupportedError ('Este navegador no permite grabar audio.' / 'Este navegador no permite capturar pestañas.' / 'No se pudo empezar a grabar.'), NoAudioTrackError ('No se compartió audio. Activa «Compartir audio» al elegir la pestaña.'), RecorderError ('La grabación se interrumpió.'). Show the permission-denied state when name === 'NotAllowedError'.
- isMicSupported(). isTabCaptureSupported() is true only on desktop Chromium (false on touch devices): use it to gate the 'Pestaña' action.
TRANSCRIBE (import ONLY from src/engine/transcribe/index.ts; never import worker.ts, decode.ts, params.ts or onsets.ts from app code, or tfjs ends up in the main bundle):
- transcribe(samples, { sensitivity, minNoteMs }, onProgress?(fraction, stage)) -> TranscribeJob { promise: Promise<NoteEvent[]>, cancel() }. Pass the settings values. The calibrated defaults are DEFAULT_TRANSCRIBE_OPTIONS (new export) = DEFAULT_SETTINGS = { sensitivity: 0.5, minNoteMs: 90 }. Sensitivity 0 keeps only confident notes; 1 gives about twice as many. minNoteMs works best between 60 and 110; above ~130 ms real sixteenth notes start to drop.
- Progress is monotonic: 'loading-model' 0-0.1 (0..0.08 while the model downloads; jumps straight to 0.1 when preloaded), 'analyzing' 0.1-0.9, 'extracting-notes' 0.9-1. Labels: Preparando / Escuchando / Escribiendo.
- Result: NoteEvent[] sorted by start (pitch 21..108, velocity 0..1). Times are in seconds from the FIRST sample you pass, so for toModelInput(buffer, range) they are relative to range.start (durationSec = range length). [] means no notes were detected (show 'No se detectaron notas' + 'Reintentar').
- Rejections: name 'TranscriptionError' with one of 'No se pudo cargar el modelo de transcripción.', 'No se pudo transcribir el audio.', 'No se pudo iniciar la transcripción en este navegador.' or 'La transcripción se detuvo de forma inesperada. Inténtalo de nuevo.'. cancel() rejects the promise with a DOMException named 'AbortError': ignore that one in the UI.
- cancel() terminates the single shared worker, which aborts every job in flight. The next call recreates the worker and reloads the model from cache. Call cancel() on ProcessingScreen unmount and on its close button. Under React StrictMode, cancelling the first effect run and then running again works. The samples are copied to the worker, not transferred, so you can keep using them.
- preloadModel() is idempotent and never rejects: call it once when Home mounts, at idle time. Also available: isModelReady(), getTranscriberBackend() ('webgl' | 'cpu' | null) and disposeTranscriber().
- Expect a first model load + warm-up of 4-10 s on a desktop GPU (likely longer on phones). After that it runs at ~30x real time on a desktop GPU, ~1.4x on software WebGL and ~0.7x on the CPU backend, so the progress bar matters on mobile.
TOOLS:
- node scripts/fixtures/check-transcription.mjs runs every fixture and prints the table and means; it exits 1 if scale F1 < 0.9. It starts its own Vite server on 5182 (or pass --url). Options: --sweep, --sweep-sensitivity, --gpu, --swiftshader, --backend cpu, --perf N, --mic, --dump dir, --only list, --verbose.
- node scripts/fixtures/check-bundle.mjs [--out dir] runs a throwaway build of the app + an engine probe and prints PASS/FAIL for 'worker is its own chunk and tfjs stays out of every other chunk'. Phase C can re-run it after capture imports the transcriber; a normal npm run build should then also show assets/worker-*.js.
- node scripts/fixtures/make-piano-fixtures.mjs regenerates the real-piano fixtures (deterministic; needs only ffmpeg).

known_issues: These are inherent Basic Pitch limits on real piano, not decoder bugs. Octave ghosts appear: the 2nd harmonic of bass notes, e.g. C4 above a C2+C3 left-hand octave. Inner chord notes that coincide with harmonics of a low octave get masked, e.g. E4 over A1/A2 or F4 over F1/F2. Real-piano block chords therefore reach F1 0.76-0.80. I measured amplitude and onset ratios of the ghosts against true octaves and they overlap, so no octave filter was added (it would delete real octaves).

Synthetic chords.wav went from 1.00 to 0.93: four G4 inner notes have frame activation ~0.33 and are now too short at the calibrated frame threshold of 0.30. This trade buys +0.085 mean F1 on real piano. Sensitivity 0.7 recovers them.
On this Windows PC, headless Chrome uses the hardware GPU by default (ANGLE D3D11, RTX 2060), not SwiftShader. Use --swiftshader to measure the software path. Phone inference speed was not measured.
The first model load costs 4-10 s on a desktop GPU because of shader compilation, so call preloadModel() early on Home.
